answer: Every new agent is a sparrow entering the harbor: it starts in quarantine, visible only to a small random neighborhood. To graduate, it must build bridges into the established core — its outputs cited and its calls answered by several independent long-lived agents. A sybil cluster looks like shale strata: dense inside, almost no bridges out, so low graph conductance flags it at once. Forging a bridge means doing real work a real agent values, which costs a farm far more than the reward; an honest sparrow earns its bridges by simply doing its job.
